name: RESTinio
baseline: Restbed v4.6 (also compared against C++ REST SDK v2.10.15, Crow v0.1, cpp-httplib v0.5.8, Pistache v0.0.002 in the same table)
workload: Same JSON echo service (POST /test) written in six C++ REST frameworks; 10 producer threads each send 1000 messages (N=1000) with 0 ms simulated handling time, client and service on one machine; time from first request to last reply, with the service on 28 threads (C=28) or 4 threads (C=4).
claimed_speedup: Local, N=1000, t=0 ms: C=28 Restinio 1.025 s vs Restbed 1.333 s (about 1.3x faster, derived from page data); C=4 Restinio 0.85 s vs Restbed 1.789 s (about 2.1x faster, derived from page data). The README states Restinio was 'over 3 times faster than the worst Cpp-REST-SDK' (3.401 s vs 1.025 s) and best of the six in these cases. With 200 ms handling time all frameworks are within a few percent.
compiler_and_flags: Not stated; services built with cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
hardware: 28x Intel Xeon CPU E5-2660 v4 @ 2.0 GHz, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu 16.04.3 LTS
tradeoffs: Header-only C++17 on standalone ASIO or Boost.ASIO, but depends on the non-header-only nodejs/llhttp. Asynchronous request handling with HTTP pipelining, ExpressJS-style router, TLS, compression, sendfile and basic WebSocket. The independent benchmark author scored it lowest for ease of including (dependency problems on Ubuntu Xenial via apt, restinio issue #86) and middling for ease of use.
caveats: Independent third-party comparison (guteksan/REST-CPP-benchmark, 130 stars) by someone not on the Restinio team; code for all six services is public but the compiler and flags are not stated and the results are a screenshot (images/rest_all.PNG) read from the image, not a text table. Single run per cell, no error bars; Restinio v0.6.2 and Restbed v4.6 are 2020-era versions, and the host is a 2016 Xeon on Ubuntu 16.04. The win only appears in the no-delay 'sprint' cases; with 200 ms handling time (N=200 and N=1000) Restinio ties the other frameworks within about 1 percent, and over a VPN the t=0 ms cases are dominated by network overhead (1:48 to 1:55 for all). The benchmark has no Restbed-specific tuning. The 'Restbed' row is also the AGPL project, so beating it is a weaker result than beating Crow or Pistache (Pistache 1.059 s and Crow 1.536 s at C=28, Pistache 0.964 s at C=4, so the margin over those is only 3 percent to 12 percent). Search snippets of a Jami issue (git.jami.net, blocked here) report Restinio at 18,834 req/s vs Restbed 12,677 req/s (ab, 10,000 requests, concurrency 20); not opened, snippet only.

name: rpclib
baseline: gRPC (also Apache Thrift and Cap'n Proto RPC in the same suite)
workload: Google Benchmark microbenchmarks of one RPC call over a local TCP socket: get_answer (return an int) and get_structs (return a large nested struct with bad alignment), five repetitions of at least 3 s each.
claimed_speedup: get_answer: rpclib 22,115 ns vs gRPC 54,841 ns (about 2.5x faster, derived from page data), vs Cap'n Proto 36,292 ns (about 1.6x); get_structs: rpclib 8,305,870 ns vs gRPC 17,676,102 ns (about 2.1x faster, derived from page data) and vs Thrift 11,648,059 ns (about 1.4x). Not faster than Thrift on get_answer (10,285 ns) nor Cap'n Proto on get_structs (183,415 ns).
compiler_and_flags: g++ 5.4 or later or clang 3.8 or later, CMake Release (-O3 default, -O2 via USE_O2), C++14; exact compiler version not stated
hardware: 4 CPUs at 2807 MHz (from the JSON context, CPU frequency scaling enabled); CPU model not stated; Arch Linux or Ubuntu 16.04; run on 2017-02-20
tradeoffs: msgpack-RPC wire protocol (interoperable with any msgpack-rpc implementation), no IDL and no code generation. The README says the library is looking for maintainers and points to packio for JSON-RPC and async. No streaming, no TLS.
caveats: First-party benchmark (rpclib/benchmarks, written by the rpclib author, who says the other libraries may be set up suboptimally) with public code but no CPU model and no exact compiler version, so tier C. Numbers date from February 2017 and use 2017-era gRPC, Thrift and Cap'n Proto versions through conan packages. gRPC has no get_blob rows in benchmark.json. On get_blob rpclib is mixed: 23,608 ns at 1 KB vs Thrift 14,362 ns and Cap'n Proto 37,791 ns, and 16,482,465 ns at 16 MB vs Cap'n Proto 13,364,192 ns and Thrift 15,126,944 ns (rpclib slower than Thrift and Cap'n Proto for most blob sizes above 256 KB). The gRPC comparison is the only one rpclib wins across the board. The accompanying blog post (szelei.me) is blocked here and was not read.
